what: Intercontinental Exchange owns exchanges and market data businesses. It runs the New York Stock Exchange, energy and interest-rate futures markets, bond pricing services and most of the software used to process US mortgages.
customers: Banks, asset managers, energy traders, listed companies and US mortgage lenders.
money: futures, options and equity trading, clearing and listings
software that processes US mortgage applications and closings
moat: Liquidity concentrated in its futures markets, and in mortgages a workflow system most US lenders already run on.
risks: Mortgage technology revenue depends on US housing activity, which high rates have suppressed
Acquisitions left debt of about $24 billion
Exchange volumes fall in calm markets
Regulators watch exchange and clearing fees closely
opportunities: Energy futures volumes have grown with volatile global gas and power markets
A recovery in US mortgage volumes would lift the most depressed part of the business
Recurring data subscriptions now make a large share of revenue predictable
watch: US mortgage origination volumes and energy futures open interest.
